reasoning: docs/DESIGN.md R12 + open decision 4. Today `ask` surfaces ONE next subject and `status` names the thin decisions, but nothing closes the loop: a low-confidence decision never becomes the specific next question, and nothing enforces a ceiling on how many questions a run may ask. The skill's governor says the budget is real, so the program must enforce it rather than trust the agent. Scope: (a) pick the thinnest decision(s), (b) derive the specific follow-up question, (c) JEV `already_answered` gate before asking, (d) a run ceiling with an explicit budget-thin marker, (e) write the question row so the branch is trackable. Acceptance: a run with a 0.41-confidence decision produces a named follow-up question, refuses one JEV scores as already answered (>= 0.55), and stops at the ceiling with `budget-thin: true` recorded rather than silently truncating.
title: [P1] the feedback engine: turn low-confidence decisions into the next question batch, bounded by a budget governor

reasoning: docs/DESIGN.md - the engine shape. The question->answer->question tree currently has no edges: `decision.question_id` exists but nothing populates it, and there is no way to ask which questions a decision closed or which new questions it opened. Without those edges the cascade cannot be walked, so depth cannot be reported honestly and a branch cannot be shown as closed. Scope: populate question_id on answer, add a `closes` list on the decision, add a walk that reports open branches and their depth. Acceptance: after answering, the decision names the question it closed; `status` reports open-branch count and max depth from the stored edges alone (no inference from prose).
title: [P1] branch linking: record that THIS answer closes THAT question, and follow the chain when a resolved answer spawns a new branch

reasoning: docs/DESIGN.md R11 + open decision 5. `dump --config` renders a hypothetical configuration but nothing judges it, so the last mile of the original ask is missing. Scope: a `verdict` verb that pipes a dump to a judge (JEV `score` against a rubric, or a large-context model for free-text critique) and writes the verdict with its reasons against the project. Acceptance: a dump with a contradiction against the recorded reasons produces a verdict that names that contradiction; the verdict is stored, not just printed.
title: [P2] verdict: hand a dump to a model (or JEV) and record good/bad with reasons

reasoning: docs/DESIGN.md R8/R13 and the skill's domain grid. The `domain` table is declared but empty, so coverage cannot be reported and the 44-domain rule from the skill is unenforced in the program. Scope: seed domains 4.01-4.44 with names, triage (blast_radius x uncertainty x irreversibility), ring floor, NOT-REACHED reason/owner/trigger/containment; report answered vs NOT-REACHED and terminating ring per domain. Acceptance: `status` prints per-domain coverage; a domain with no rows is reported as absent rather than silently omitted (silence and 'does not apply' are different claims).
title: [P2] seed the 44-domain grid as real rows with triage scores, and report coverage and depth per domain

reasoning: docs/DESIGN.md v0.2 list. The spec currently exists only as JSONL rows plus a per-decision dump; a reader cannot get the whole project in one pass, and a downstream agent has no single artifact to consume. Scope: `export` that renders project, core statement, every decision with why-not, the option set, escalations, unknowns and assumptions to one markdown document. Acceptance: exporting a namespace reproduces every decision and its why_not; the output is stable across runs (no unordered dict bleed).
title: [P3] export: render a whole namespace to one readable spec document

reasoning: tests/smoke.sh proves the loop end to end (15 assertions, green) but it is a shell script: it cannot assert on internal behaviour, it leaves its namespace behind, and it cannot run a single case. The verbs are the API now that the repo is public, so they need real regression coverage. Scope: pytest suite that creates a namespace, exercises every verb, asserts on stored rows (not just stdout), and tears the namespace down even on failure. Acceptance: `pytest` green from a clean checkout; a deliberately broken verb fails exactly one named test.
title: [P2] a pytest suite against an ephemeral namespace, replacing shell-only coverage
